identity.identity_result: The pinned contract and every constituent source hash match the implementation reports. The aggregate source_manifest_sha256 has no separately stored manifest or declared canonicalization rule, so the constituent hashes are the independently reproducible identity.

findings.requirement: The executor request is declared ready/valid, must remain stable under backpressure, and must compose with a legal ready/valid consumer.
findings.finding: The source waits for executor ready in CHECK_READY before entering ISSUE and asserting valid. A consumer that legally waits to see valid before asserting ready can therefore deadlock forever. The existing backpressure test does not cover this case: it raises ready first, waits for valid, and only then lowers ready. The frozen contract is internally ambiguous because it names ready_valid while its issue_rule also requires executor ready before issue; the RTL follows the latter wording but is not safely composable under ordinary ready/valid semantics.
findings.raw_evidence: Static cycle trace: with dma_cmd_ready/gemm_cmd_ready held low, state_r remains CHECK_READY and both request valids remain low. No handshake can occur if the consumer waits for valid.
findings.retry_owner: Parent contract owner and isa_command_dispatcher implementation owner

findings.requirement: Illegal operands enter ERROR; a GEMM requires ready source banks and a free destination bank; active banks cannot be overwritten.
findings.finding: GEMM does not reject dst_bank equal to src0_bank or src1_bank. Such an alias passes operands_legal_w but can never pass banks_ready_w because the same bank must be READY and FREE simultaneously. With a strict single PC and no external bank-state transition, the command remains busy forever instead of being rejected. src0_bank equal to src1_bank is executable and its duplicate release writes are benign, but destination/source alias is a permanent stall. The frozen contract does not explicitly state the bank-distinctness rule, so this is both a contract gap and an unsafe RTL liveness behavior.
findings.raw_evidence: Static condition proof: for dst==src0 or dst==src1, banks_ready_w contains BANK_READY && BANK_FREE on one bank-state register, which is unsatisfiable.
findings.retry_owner: Parent ISA/module-contract owner and isa_command_dispatcher implementation owner

findings.requirement: Bind interface payload, boundaries, rollback/release, and reset behavior to self-checking dynamic evidence.
findings.finding: The self-checking testbench proves the main strict-order trace, one DMA backpressure trace, no-lookahead, zero/1025 count rejection, load failure, tag mismatch, selected reset phases, and repeated runs. It does not compare every 256-bit issued command against the corresponding BRAM instruction or independent model; does not run command_count=1024 through PC 1023/address 2047; does not test a consumer that withholds ready until valid; does not test GEMM backpressure or GEMM source-release flags; does not test DMA_STORE failure rollback or GEMM failure rollback; and does not explicitly reset in both fetch phases and CHECK_READY. The three-case Python model is not connected to RTL output comparison and does not cover those cases.
findings.raw_evidence: Independent XSIM rerun passes the existing suite, but source audit shows only tag checks for most requests and only a held-value stability check for the first DMA request.
findings.promotion_effect: blocking until P1 fixes are covered; thereafter required before integration promotion

verified_behaviors.synchronous_one_cycle_bram_fetch: Source inspection and passing XSIM show lower-word then upper-word assembly with a one-cycle memory model. Each word is deliberately captured one cycle after the modeled BRAM updates cmd_mem_rdata; this is conservative but correct for the declared one-cycle synchronous read.
verified_behaviors.strict_next_fetch: Verified by RTL transition audit and the dynamic outstanding/fetch monitor: the next FETCH_LO is entered only on a matching successful completion handshake.
verified_behaviors.pc_update: PC increments once only on matching successful non-final completion; final completion retains the last command index and enters DONE.
verified_behaviors.one_outstanding: Structurally enforced by ISSUE to WAIT_COMPLETION and dynamically checked by the testbench monitor.
verified_behaviors.bank_reservation: Reservations occur on request valid-and-ready acceptance; load/GEMM destination failure becomes FAULT and DMA_STORE failure returns source to READY. Main-path DMA_STORE release is dynamically covered; other release/rollback combinations lack dynamic coverage as recorded above.
verified_behaviors.command_count_rejection: 0 and 1025 are dynamically rejected. The accepted upper boundary 1024 is structurally representable but not dynamically exercised.
verified_behaviors.reset: Synchronous reset clears state, PC, captured command, terminal error, and all bank states. Existing dynamic coverage does not distinctly prove every active FSM state.
verified_behaviors.timing_exception_legitimacy: Accepted for module-only post-synthesis OOC scope. The two false-hold constraints originate only at non-clock input ports or terminate only at output ports. Independent OOC rerun retains 324 internal register-to-register hold paths, with worst internal path pc_r_reg[4]/Q to pc_r_reg[4]/D and WHS 0.084 ns. No DUT reg-to-reg hold path is excluded by these endpoint-scoped exceptions. External I/O, placement, route, and board timing remain unproven.
